[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#rad-scope]

### RAD Scope

This document covers:
- VPC/account segmentation architecture for production cloud environments
- Security group and private endpoint governance patterns
- Inter-environment connectivity design
- Infrastructure-as-code governance patterns for cloud network security

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#capability-domain-boundary]

### Capability Domain Boundary

Cloud Network Security governs the network architecture within and between cloud environments. It begins at the cloud account/subscription boundary and extends to all network constructs within cloud environments. It interfaces with:

- **Microsegmentation ABB** (GUID-SEC-NETWORK-MICROSEG-2.2.03): Security groups are the cloud-native realization of microsegmentation policy
- **Network Monitoring ABB** (GUID-SEC-NETWORK-NETMON-2.2.10): VPC flow logs are the cloud-native network telemetry source
- **Perimeter Firewall ABB** (GUID-SEC-NETWORK-FIREWALL-2.2.01): Cloud-native firewall services (e.g., AWS Network Firewall) operate at the VPC boundary as the cloud-native perimeter control

### Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Account_Structure["Cloud Account / Subscription Structure"]
        subgraph Network_Account["Network / Connectivity Account"]
            TGW[Transit Gateway]
            NGFW[Cloud Network Firewall\nPerimeter Control]
            EGRESS[Egress Inspection Point\nTraffic Control ABB]
        end

        subgraph Prod_VPC["Production VPC"]
            subgraph Public_Tier["Public Subnet Tier"]
                ALB[Application Load Balancer\n+ WAF]
            end
            subgraph App_Tier["Application Subnet Tier"]
                APP_SG[Application Workloads\nSecurity Group: App Tier]
            end
            subgraph Data_Tier["Data Subnet Tier"]
                DATA_SG[Data Services\nSecurity Group: Data Tier]
            end
            subgraph Endpoint_Tier["Service Endpoints"]
                PVTE[Private Service Endpoints\nS3, Secrets, ECR, etc.]
            end
        end

        subgraph Shared_VPC["Shared Services VPC"]
            DNS_R[Governed DNS Resolver\nDNS Security ABB]
            MONITOR[Flow Log Collection\nNetwork Monitoring ABB]
        end
    end

    Internet --> NGFW --> TGW --> ALB
    ALB --> APP_SG
    APP_SG --> DATA_SG
    APP_SG --> PVTE
    DATA_SG --> PVTE

    TGW --> EGRESS

    App_Tier -.->|VPC Flow Logs| MONITOR
    Data_Tier -.->|VPC Flow Logs| MONITOR
    APP_SG -.->|DNS Queries| DNS_R
    DATA_SG -.->|DNS Queries| DNS_R
    MONITOR --> SIEM[Enterprise SIEM\nSecOps Domain]
```

*All component names are logical — not vendor or product names.*
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#logical-components]

### Logical Components

| Component | Type | Architectural Role |
|---|---|---|
| Network / Connectivity Account | Logical Boundary | Centralized account for shared network infrastructure; isolates network controls from workload accounts |
| Transit Gateway | Integration Point | Managed hub connecting VPCs and hybrid connectivity; explicit route tables govern inter-VPC communication |
| Cloud Network Firewall | ABB — GUID-SEC-NETWORK-FIREWALL-2.2.01 | Stateful traffic inspection at VPC perimeter; enforces north-south and inter-VPC policy |
| Application Load Balancer + WAF | ABB — GUID-SEC-NETWORK-WAF-2.2.02 | Layer-7 traffic termination and web application filtering for internet-facing services |
| Security Groups (per tier) | Logical Control | Workload-level microsegmentation; enforces tier isolation and minimal permitted flows |
| Private Service Endpoints | Logical Control | Private network paths to cloud-managed services; eliminates public internet exposure for service access |
| Governed DNS Resolver | ABB — GUID-SEC-NETWORK-DNS-SEC-2.2.08 | Enterprise DNS resolver with threat filtering; all VPC workloads resolve through this service |
| VPC Flow Log Collection | ABB — GUID-SEC-NETWORK-NETMON-2.2.10 | Network telemetry pipeline from cloud flow logs to SIEM |

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#pattern-1-three-tier-vpc-segmentation]

### Pattern 1: Three-Tier VPC Segmentation

**When to use**: Production workloads with public-facing components and sensitive data tier.

**Logical flow**:
1. Internet traffic terminates at the public subnet load balancer with WAF inline
2. Application tier security group permits inbound traffic only from the load balancer's security group on defined application ports
3. Data tier security group permits inbound traffic only from the application tier security group on defined data service ports
4. All service access (cloud storage, secrets, container registry) uses private endpoints; no outbound internet access from application or data tiers

**Infrastructure-as-code pattern**: Security group rules defined as code; policy-as-code gate validates no 0.0.0.0/0 inbound rules on application or data tier security groups before apply
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#pattern-2-hub-and-spoke-inter-environment-connectivity]

### Pattern 2: Hub-and-Spoke Inter-Environment Connectivity

**When to use**: Multi-account or multi-environment deployments requiring controlled inter-VPC communication.

**Logical flow**:
1. All inter-VPC traffic routes through the transit gateway in the network account
2. Transit gateway route tables define explicit permitted routes between environments; no implicit full-mesh routing
3. Traffic between environments traverses the cloud network firewall in the network account for inspection
4. Hybrid connectivity (VPN/Direct Connect) terminates at the transit gateway; on-premises routes are explicitly propagated
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#pattern-3-service-mesh-for-container-to-container-security]

### Pattern 3: Service Mesh for Container-to-Container Security

**When to use**: Container platforms with significant inter-service API traffic requiring mTLS and service authorization.

**Logical flow**:
1. Service mesh data plane agents are deployed alongside each application service
2. All inter-service communication is intercepted by the data plane, which enforces mTLS between services
3. Service-to-service authorization policy defines which services may communicate with which other services
4. Service mesh telemetry (connection metadata, error rates, latency) is forwarded to the monitoring pipeline

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#deployment-context-considerations]

## Deployment Context Considerations

| Context | Architectural Consideration |
|---|---|
| AWS (Platform Gainwell) | AWS Network Firewall for VPC perimeter; AWS Transit Gateway for hub-and-spoke; VPC Interface Endpoints for private service access; VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch or S3 for monitoring |
| Multi-region | Regional network accounts with inter-region transit gateway peering; consistent security group policy enforced through infrastructure-as-code across regions |
| Hybrid (cloud + data center) | Transit gateway with Direct Connect or VPN attachment; explicit route advertisement governance; consistent security policy intent expressed in both environments |

page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CLOUD-NET-RAD-3.2.03.md#constraints-and-exceptions]

## Constraints and Exceptions

- Security group rules that permit broad inter-tier access (e.g., permitting all traffic from one account CIDR to another) are architectural anti-patterns; exceptions require documented justification and compensating monitoring controls
- Service mesh adoption in environments with legacy applications may require phased rollout; applications that cannot support sidecar injection require alternative inter-service security patterns
- VPC flow logs provide flow-level metadata only; deep packet inspection requires deployment of cloud-native network firewall with stateful inspection at VPC boundaries
